Cabinet reshuffle draws mixed reactions, more changes may be coming
item.description:
The government has carried out its first cabinet reshuffle six months into its term. Shortly after Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as president on Friday, three new full ministers and two state ministers took oath.

One state minister was promoted to full minister. At the same time, one minister was given a different portfolio, while another was removed from the cabinet and appointed as an adviser to the prime minister with the rank of a minister.

The reshuffle has drawn mixed reactions in political and administrative circles. Some people close to the government see it as an initial outcome of the prime minister’s promised six-month performance review. Others view it as an effort to fill several vacant posts, redistribute portfolios and improve political coordination.

Meanwhile, discussions have already begun about another cabinet reorganisation. A responsible source at the Prime Minister’s Office said further changes could come within a few weeks. However, discussions in political and administrative circles suggest that the next round could be delayed until September.

The biggest question raised by this reshuffle concerns the structure of the cabinet. Following the expansion and redistribution of portfolios, several ministries now have a minister, a state minister and a prime minister’s adviser overseeing matters related to the same ministry. Questions have also been raised about why both a full minister and a state minister have been appointed to several relatively small ministries.

Cabinet reshuffle, five new members, who will get which ministry

The issue of austerity has also come into the discussion. The prime minister’s personal frugality has sent a positive message to the government and administration. On the other hand, there is debate over whether the expansion of the cabinet contradicts that message to some extent.

After Friday’s changes, the cabinet has 51 members, including the prime minister. There are 26 full ministers and 24 state ministers besides the prime minister. Outside the cabinet, there are 10 advisers to the prime minister—six with the rank of minister and five with the rank of state minister.

Cabinet reshuffle: Gazette issued, who gets which ministry

According to the Cabinet Division’s list, advisers with the rank of minister include Nazrul Islam Khan, who is in charge of the Ministry of Agriculture, and Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, who oversees the Ministry of Industries.

Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir is responsible for the ministries of Finance and Planning, while Ismail Jabiullah oversees Public Administration. Among the advisers with the rank of state minister, Humaiun Kobir had been responsible for the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Disaster Management and Relief, and Civil Aviation and Tourism.

After taking oath as a state minister on 21 August, his responsibilities have changed. It has not yet been announced whether he will continue as adviser to the prime minister for the other two ministries. Zahir Uddin Swapan has newly been appointed political adviser with the rank of minister.

Foreign Affairs gets a minister and two state ministers

Following the latest changes, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has one full minister and two state ministers. It is unprecedented for a ministry to have two state ministers. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman already had Shama Obaed Islam as a state minister. Humaiun Kobir has now joined her. Their respective responsibilities have not yet been announced separately.

Home Minister and BNP Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed told Prothom Alo on Saturday, “There is no problem with having several state ministers in a ministry. For example, in the United States, alongside the secretary of state there are deputy secretaries of state and undersecretaries. To speed up government work, more than one state minister can work alongside the minister at the Foreign Affairs Ministry. This exists in the governments of various countries.”

Small ministries also have ministers, state ministers and advisers

Several relatively small ministries, in terms of their size, activities and budgets, now have a minister, a state minister and an adviser. Some even have special assistants.

The Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment is relatively small, yet it now has a minister, a state minister and an adviser with the rank of state minister. There is also a special assistant to the prime minister, with the rank of secretary, responsible for overseas employment in the Asia-Pacific region. His name is Md Shakirul Islam Khan.

Ariful Haque Chowdhury is the minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, while Nurul Haque is the state minister. Mahdi Amin is the prime minister’s adviser for the ministry. He is also responsible for three other ministries—Education, Primary and Mass Education, and Labour and Employment.

The Ministry of Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs had remained without a full minister for more than two and a half months. Saching Prue Jerry, a representative of the hill communities, has now been made a full minister. Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin was already serving there as state minister. The ministry has traditionally been headed by representatives of ethnic minority communities. This time, however, a state minister from outside the hill communities has been appointed alongside the full minister. Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin is also serving as state minister for the Ministry of Land.

Kazi Shah Mofazzal Houssain Kaikobad was already serving as minister for Religious Affairs. Mohammad Shamim Kaiser has now been appointed state minister. Muslim clerics from Hefazat-e-Islam and other groups in the same ideological camp have already issued statements objecting to his appointment.

The ministries of Information and Broadcasting, Culture, Planning, as well as Primary and Mass Education also now have three levels of political leadership—a minister, a state minister and an adviser. The ministries of Health and Environment have ministers and state ministers as well as subject-specific special assistants.

Contrasts from one ministry to another

In the latest reshuffle, Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) chairman Andaleeve Rahman Partho, an ally of the BNP in its electoral alliance, was appointed information and broadcasting minister. Some see this as a reflection of political partnership. However, the reason Zahir Uddin Swapan was removed from the ministry remains unclear.

Zahed Ur Rahman is serving as an adviser with the rank of state minister for the ministries of Information and Broadcasting and Culture. Yasser Khan Choudhury is also a state minister in the same ministry.

By contrast, one full minister, Sheikh Robiul Alam, is responsible for three major ministries—Road Transport and Bridges, Railways, and Shipping. He has two state ministers working alongside him, Habibur Rashid and Md Rajib Ahsan.

One full minister is also responsible for the Ministries of Industries, Commerce, and Textiles and Jute. The Finance and Planning ministries have a minister, a state minister and an adviser with the rank of minister.

Md Aminur Rashid is the minister for Agriculture and Livestock. Sultan Salahuddin is serving as state minister for Livestock.

These contrasts in the allocation of political leadership across ministries have sparked discussion both within and outside the BNP, as well as in the wider public sphere.

Has the six-month performance review begun?

Many see the first cabinet reshuffle as a result of the government’s performance over its first six months. At the beginning of his government, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced a 180-day action plan.

The prime minister’s information adviser, Zahir Uddin Swapan, also recently said that a committee comprising advisers and special assistants at the Prime Minister’s Office was reviewing the achievements, activities and limitations of various ministries during their first 180 days.

In other words, there is little doubt that the six-month performance review has begun. However, Friday’s reshuffle cannot yet be described as the complete outcome of that review. The government has not disclosed the criteria used to assess ministers and state ministers, which ministers performed well or poorly against which indicators, or why particular portfolios were changed.

There has been discussion within the government that seven or eight ministries have not been progressing as expected. However, that appears to have had only a limited impact on this round of changes. For this reason, some people close to the government regard the reshuffle as the “first phase” of the six-month performance review.

After the reshuffle, Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury told journalists that the cabinet’s performance would be reviewed after a certain period and changes would be made as necessary. He said there would be further evaluations in the future and more changes could be made to the cabinet.

Second round of portfolio redistribution may be next

Sources close to the government and the BNP said the cabinet could be expanded and portfolios redistributed again within the next few weeks. Several new ministers, and particularly state ministers, could be added at that time.

Portfolios could be divided among ministers who currently oversee several ministries, including Agriculture and Livestock; Commerce, Industries, and Textiles and Jute; and Railways, Road Transport and Bridges, and Shipping.

However, the matter is still under discussion. No final information is available on the possible candidates or how many new members may be added. The prime minister may make a decision based on the ongoing performance review, the government’s one-year programme, coordination between the party and the government, and regional representation.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told Prothom Alo that cabinet restructuring and redistribution of portfolios fall within the prime minister’s authority and are routine matters for a government.

The election of a party member as president naturally created a vacancy. The Ministry of Local Government is an important ministry and needs an appointment. There had also been no full minister in charge of the food portfolio.

Two more people have been appointed state ministers. “Everyone who took oath is qualified,” he said. “You could call this an assessment of six months of performance, or the first step towards running the government more efficiently.”

Approaching the size of larger cabinets in the past

Among political governments since 1991, three cabinets were larger than the current 51-member cabinet. The Awami League government’s cabinet in the 2009–14 term had 62 members. The BNP government’s cabinet in 2001–06 had 60 members, while the Awami League government’s cabinet in 2014–19 had 59.

If new members are added, the current cabinet could move even closer to the size of those three larger cabinets of the past.

As the government conducts its six-month performance review, three issues are now raising separate questions: expanding the size of the cabinet, placing multiple layers of political leadership within the same ministry, and appointing ministers and state ministers even to smaller ministries while leaving major ministries under the responsibility of a single minister.

For this reason, many people concerned with the matter view last Friday’s reshuffle not as a final reorganisation, but rather as preparation for another round of changes

item.title: New president to move into Bangabhaban today, let’s look for century-old building’s history
item.description:
Bangabhaban serves as the official residence and office of the President of Bangladesh.

Although new President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir took the oath of office at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban on Friday evening, he will move into the century-old building today, Sunday.

The British rulers constructed the building in 1905, following the announcement of the Partition of Bengal.

The partition divided Bengal into two provinces: one was West Bengal, with Calcutta as its capital, while the other was Eastern Bengal and Assam, with Dhaka as its capital.

The Partition of Bengal took effect in October 1905. The new province had been established, but where would its new Lieutenant Governor live?

To meet this need, the British Government initiated the construction of what is now Bangabhaban in Dhaka. However, the name “Bangabhaban” was given to the building only after Bangladesh gained independence.

Sir Joseph Bamfylde Fuller came to Dhaka as the first Lieutenant Governor of the newly created Eastern Bengal and Assam province.

The authorities began constructing a new official residence for him in the Dilkusha area, at a site known as Dana Dighi Maidan. Construction began in 1905 and was completed in 1911. Fuller moved into the new residence as early as 1906, before construction was fully completed.

Historian Muntassir Mamoon provides a detailed account of Bangabhaban’s construction in the second volume of his book “Dhaka Smriti Bismriti Nagari”.

President pays tribute at National Memorial

The history is also documented in Dhaka Kosh, published by the Asiatic Society of Bangladesh.

According to these books, the site where Bangabhaban now stands once belonged to the Nawab family of Dhaka.

After the Partition of Bengal, when the British Government expressed interest in building a residence for the Lieutenant Governor, Nawab Sir Salimullah proposed constructing it in the family garden at Dilkusha. The Nawab family subsequently leased the southern part of the garden to the British Government for this purpose.

The authorities chose the section of the southern part known as “Dana Dighi Maidan” as the site for the building. Bamfylde Fuller himself selected the location for the residence.

Until the annulment of the Partition of Bengal in 1911, the Legislative Council of the Eastern Bengal and Assam province held its meetings there. The building also hosted receptions for members of the elite on various occasions.

Later, the building became the venue for the swearing-in ceremonies of the chief minister and ministers of Eastern Bengal. Officials also organised programmes there to mark important national occasions at Government House, now known as Bangabhaban.

According to Dhaka Kosh, even after the annulment of the Partition of Bengal, a provision remained in place requiring the provincial governor to visit and stay in Dhaka during a specific period each year. The Government House at Dilkusha served this purpose at the time.

From timber palace to Bangabhaban

According to Dhaka Kosh, construction of the present-day building began in 1905 on a 23.5-hectare site and was completed in 1911. Initially, authorities named it “Government House”.

The teak-built structure had a floor area of 25,128 square feet, with its wooden floor raised four feet above the ground. This led people to call it the “Timber Palace.”

A cyclone damaged the timber palace in 1961, leaving it completely unfit for use.

The authorities subsequently decided to construct a new residence for the Governor of then East Pakistan. To design the new building, they brought renowned architect Moinuddin Chishti from Lahore.

At the request of the then Governor, Azam Khan, Moinuddin Chishti incorporated Islamic architectural elements prominently into the design.

The architect completed construction of the 84,000-square-foot, two-storey building on 17 January 1964. The new palace featured a Darbar Hall, the Governor’s bedroom and office, as well as several rooms for hosting various functions.

Meanwhile, the second volume of “Dhaka Smriti Bismriti Nagari” states that an air raid damaged the building during the Great Liberation War in 1971. The authorities subsequently carried out further renovations.

After Bangladesh gained independence on 16 December, the first Cabinet meeting of the new country took place here on 23 December.

At the time, the authorities designated the building as the official residence and office of the President and named it Bangabhaban.

Over the years, additional rooms have been added to Bangabhaban to meet changing needs. The interior has also been adorned with paintings by some of the country’s renowned artists.

item.title: Starc heroics see Australia thrash Bangladesh
item.description:
CRICKET-AUS-BAN

An irrepressible Mitchell Starc bagged four wickets and 10 for the match as he ripped through the Bangladesh batting to ensure a commanding innings and 51-run second Test victory for Australia inside two days on Sunday.

The visitors headed into the Mackay showdown on a high after shocking the world's top-ranked team by nine wickets in the first Test at Darwin.

But they were brought crashing back to earth by some scintillating fast bowling, led by Starc who finished with 10-51 for the match to level the two-game series.

After 18 wickets fell on a frenetic first day in Mackay, the hosts were all out for 210 in the morning session, securing a lead of 146 on the back of Cameron Green's 67.

Records galore on first day of Mackay Test

Star Bangladesh quick Shoriful Islam claimed 7-48 -- the best figures from a Bangladeshi bowler in an away Test.

The visitors crashed for just 64 in their first innings, when Starc took 6-12, and he was the chief tormentor again, claiming 4-39 while Pat Cummins took 3-10 and Nathan Lyon 3-25.

Bangladesh had a horror start with Shadman Islam lasting just three balls, playing a nothing stroke to a moving Starc delivery and edging to Marnus Labuschagne at point.

Mominul Haque was equally clueless next ball, failing to offer a shot with Starc removing his off stump and setting up a hat-trick opportunity.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, who was out for a golden duck in the first innings, this time survived to deny Starc.

But their woes deepened when Tanzid Hasan departed soon after for nine. Starc was again involved, taking a catch in the deep after Tanzid pulled Cummins.

Shanto did well to soak up the pressure after lunch for 46 deliveries, but he eventually lost focus against the off-spin of Nathan Lyon, holing out to the safe hands of Starc at long off on 31.

And when Starc was brought back into the attack, he was front and centre again, enticing a loose shot from Litton Das who was caught without scoring by Beau Webster at third slip.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz struggled to get going and departed to an equally poor shot, lashing at a Cummins bouncer and collected by wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

Starc finishes with six as Bangladesh all out for 64 in first innings of second test v Australia

The Australian captain then removed Hasan Mahmud (two) before Starc took his 10th for the match -- the fourth time he has achieved the feat -- when he bowled Taijul Islam for seven.

Lyon quickly wrapped up the tail in the first over after tea.

Australia resumed at 165-8 with Green on 51 and Lyon on 10.

Green, who scored a century during the first Test in Darwin, kept the scoreboard moving early with quick singles.

But he was undone by an inswinging yorker from the impressive Shoriful that hit him on the toe with a review declaring him out lbw.

A valiant Lyon brought up the 200 for Australia with a towering six off Taskin and with Josh Hazlewood adding 24 crucial runs for the last wicket.

The innings ended when Hazlewood skied Taijul to Shadman on six to leave Lyon not out 32.

item.title: Inter thrash Monza to launch Serie A title defence
item.description:
Inter Milan kicked off the defence of their Serie A title in emphatic fashion on Saturday, cruising to a 4-1 home victory over promoted Monza.
The reigning Italian champions needed just six minutes to break the deadlock when Hakan Calhanoglu blasted in from distance.
Monza, back in the top flight after a season in Serie B, levelled through Gustavo Varela in the 29th minute.
Inter restored their advantage shortly after the restart, with Piotr Zielinski finding the net in the 48th minute.
Pio Esposito, preferred in the starting line-up to Marcus Thuram, made it 3-1 eight minutes later with an inventive backheel finish from Andy Diouf's cross.
Yann Bisseck completed the scoring in the 63rd minute as Inter underlined their status as clear favourites to retain the Scudetto.
John Stones, one of three England internationals signed by Inter during the close season, made his debut after coming on as a substitute.
"We were a bit rusty during the first half, a bit too frantic as well," Inter coach Cristian Chivu told DAZN. "We regained our calm and clarity after the break."
Napoli, who finished runners-up to Inter last season, struck two late goals to brush aside Genoa 2-0 and get new coach Massimiliano Allegri off to a winning start.
Allegri, a six-time Serie A winner as a coach, is looking to make a statement after being dismissed by AC Milan following just one season in charge.
Napoli had to wait until the 82nd minute to break the deadlock through Kevin De Bruyne, who swung the game his team's way after coming on as a second-half substitute.
The Belgium international, who missed a large chunk of his first season in Naples with a hamstring injury, then set up Antonio Vergara to add a second to wrap up the points.
"De Bruyne is an extraordinary guy. He does things that are simply different from everyone else," Allegri told Sky Sport. "He sees things that others do not see. There are very few players at that level."
Last season's surprise package Como needed a second-half equaliser from Greece forward Tasos Douvikas to earn a 1-1 draw at Udinese.
Como will play in the Champions League for the first time next month after finishing fourth under Cesc Fabregas.
Cagliari won 1-0 at Parma courtesy of Alessandro Romano's goal 11 minutes from time.
Milan and Juventus, both seeking redemption after disappointing campaigns and further summer overhauls, begin their league seasons on Sunday against Torino and Frosinone respectively.

item.title: Messi scores but Miami slump continues with loss to Toronto
item.description:
A goal from Lionel Messi wasn't enough as Inter Miami fell 2-1 at home to Toronto on Saturday for their fifth straight match without a win.
Miami trailed 2-0 after goals from Toronto's Josh Sargent and Derrick Etienne Jr. in the 59th and 62nd minutes.
Argentine superstar Messi pulled a goal back for Miami in the 82nd, capitalizing on a sensational through ball from compatriot Rodrigo De Paul.
But Miami's final siege yielded no reward.
With 14 goals Messi is second on the Major League Soccer scoring chart behind Dallas's Petar Musa -- who went into Saturday with 16.
But Miami have four losses and a draw in their last five matches. That includes MLS play and the Leagues Cup, in which they were eliminated in the group stage.
They remained in second place in the MLS Eastern Conference, seven games behind leaders Nashville who have a game in hand.
But Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire moved within three points of Miami in the standings after a 1-1 draw at New York Red Bulls on Saturday.
Orlando City moved into the MLS Cup playoff positions in the East with a 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake.
Orlando's French star Antoine Griezmann, recently arrived from Atletico Madrid, scored twice in the second half, his first MLS brace pulling Orlando back after Real Salt Lake took the lead through Dominik Marczuk in the 36th minute.

item.title: Real Madrid snatch late win at Espanyol on Mourinho's return
item.description:
Jose Mourinho's second spell in charge of Real Madrid began with a last-gasp 2-1 victory at Espanyol in La Liga on Saturday, with substitute Carlos Espi pouncing in the 90th minute to grab the winner.
Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in Los Blancos' opening fixture of the season, and new signing Espi secured the points at the death after Alex Calatrava had levelled against Mourinho's star-studded team.
"I think that we deserved to win but that Espanyol didn't deserve to lose," Mourinho told reporters.
"They didn't have any players at the World Cup and have been working together for a long time, and you could see that."
Back in charge of Madrid 13 years after leaving, Portuguese veteran Mourinho must bring the dressing room under control after the chaos of last season, and end Spanish champions Barcelona's domestic dominance.
Mourinho started with superstars Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Bellingham, as well as handing debuts to Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries and Ibrahima Konate.
Bellingham had an excellent first season at Madrid after arriving from Borussia Dortmund but the subsequent two were disappointing, both for him and the club, who failed to win a major trophy in either.
Mourinho installed him in attacking midfield with licence to roam and the former Birmingham man was heavily involved before his goal as Madrid probed.
The England international netted the first of Mourinho's second era at the club, heading home Arda Guler's dangerous crossed free-kick.
Espanyol threatened midway through the first half as Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois beat away Clemens Riedel's drive and Roberto Fernandez hooked over shortly afterwards.
Madrid did not heed the warning and Espanyol levelled in the 30th minute, Calatrava slotting home Javi Hernandez's cut-back after a fine team move.
- Intense battle -
Espanyol stopper Marko Dmitrovic made a good save to stop Mbappe after he got in behind on the right of the area.
The French forward, La Liga's top scorer in both of his two seasons at the club, was not at his lethal best in front of goal.
On the left flank Vinicius had little impact, beyond winning a series of fouls from Espanyol players who were determined to shut him down by any means.
"Vini is not a saint, but what they do to im is too much, it started in the first minute, I think it's something systemic, it's done in a systemic way," said Mourinho.
"First I hack him, then you, then me, then you, if I get a yellow then you do it. I have a yellow so I go off, and someone comes on without a yellow... it's frustrating for him."
Mourinho sent on two more new arrivals in the form of record signing Yan Diomande and Marc Cucurella as Madrid sought a winner in the final 25 minutes.
Federico Valverde hit the outside of the post with a low effort from the edge of the box as Espanyol dug deep to deny Madrid clear chances.
However in the 90th minute Madrid found the goal they needed when former Levante striker Espi, the lowest profile of Los Blancos' summer purchases, capitalised on a loose ball in the box and fired home.
"We carried out our plan well and then let in that goal at the end," said Calatrava.
"That we conceded was a gut-punch, because we worked hard until the end."
Earlier, Sevilla won 3-1 at Athletic Bilbao and Valencia and Celta Vigo drew 0-0.
